Market Signals From The Yen And US Bonds

Anatole Kaletsky

Gavekal Research | 8 Sep 2026

When it comes to financial markets, the cliché that “the market is always right” is almost exactly wrong. Not in the sense that market prices are always wrong, since most securities are correctly priced most of the time; but in the sense that there are always some assets that markets are mispricing completely. The challenge and opportunity of financial trading, as George Soros explained 40 years ago in his manifesto, The Alchemy of Finance, is to discover which assets are most out of line with their appropriate and sustainable prices at any particular time—and then make money from their realignment.This summer, three cases of mispricing escalated into what I called “market madness” (see Regime Change Can Cause Market Madness). The obvious one, which everybody has discussed, is the speculation in AI-related equities. But the two other mispricings are arguably even more important: the crazy cheapness of the yen; and the irrational faith among bond investors that the Fed will return inflation to its 2% target.
